summary:
DustPulse

DustPulse is a smart early-warning system designed to protect astronauts from the health risks of lunar and Martian dust. The idea is based on using a distributed network of tiny sensors inside spacecraft habitats to monitor dust concentration and air quality, while also tracking astronauts’ vital signs, including heart rate, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate.

The system connects environmental conditions with each astronaut’s health status to understand how dust exposure may affect their bodies. It calculates a cumulative exposure level and classifies risks into three categories: Safe, Warning, and Danger.

When a potential health risk is detected, the system generates personalized alerts based on each astronaut’s physical condition, allowing early action before the situation becomes serious. This helps astronauts monitor their health independently without relying entirely on Earth-based medical support.

DustPulse aims to improve astronaut safety during long-term space missions, especially future lunar and Mars exploration. The same concept can also be applied on Earth to monitor dust exposure in industrial workplaces, mining areas, and cities affected by sandstorms.
details: Novax DustPulse Project Summary * Project Name & Concept: * Name: DustPulse (Distributed Smart Dust System and Astronaut Health Monitoring) * Core Idea: An early-warning smart system using a distributed network of nanosensors inside spacecraft habitats to monitor dust concentration and fine particulate matter (PM_{2.5} and PM_{10}), linking them directly with astronauts' biometric indicators (respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and heart rate). * Problem Addressed: * Lunar and Martian dust pose complex health hazards (respiratory, cardiovascular, ocular, and skin effects). NASA’s exposure limit is 0.3\text{ mg/m}^3. In long-duration missions, astronauts cannot rely solely on Earth-based medical teams for real-time diagnosis. * How It Works: * Data Collection: Monitors cabin air quality and dust levels alongside crew biometric data. * Processing & Evaluation: Computes a custom Cumulative Exposure Index (CEI) via an intelligent engine, classifying risk levels (Safe, Warning, Danger) completely independently of ground control. * Interaction: Generates personalized alerts tailored to each astronaut's individual physical status (such as elevated respiration rate during exercise). * Impact & Benefits: * In Space: Protects crew health for the Artemis program and future Mars missions, supporting health independence. * On Earth: Dust monitoring technology can be adapted for industrial environments, mining, and sandstorm-affected cities (aligning with Saudi Vision 2030). * Tools & Technologies Used: * Programming & Logic: Python (for the 7-day data simulator and CEI calculation engine). * Interfaces & Applications: Streamlit (for the interactive web dashboard). * Reference Data: NASA TechPort ExAM datasets and NASA Human Research Roadmap standards.
